speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing acute diarrhea; to help you, I need to ask a few questions. How long has this been going on, and have you had any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI).

Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia and the onset of watery diarrhea with abdominal cramping, you have classic signs of antibiotic-associated colitis. I need to confirm if you have experienced any recent hospitalization or nursing home stays, and I will order a C. diff toxin assay and stool culture to confirm.
